source_binding: Every command retains source hashes, snapshots, patch, output, and terminal exit status. The final Go checks match committed Go source. The prose check matches the committed document and precedes additional tests without comments. The corrected fail-before run uses archived previous-commit production source through a Go overlay.
qualification: Local candidate handoff, publication guards, and recovery. CSP5 remains incomplete. No task acceptance, native Linux/Windows execution, PR, merge, or released-pair credit.
previous_goal_turn: Progress: source 873a53c5 and canonical 3450f36a implemented private preparation recovery. This turn revalidated both worktrees and extended ownership through candidate publication and cleanup.
limits: The original regression draft expected the old catalog after Repair received the new committed catalog. That expectation was incorrect. The corrected overlay uses base 873a53c5 and proves abandoned candidates before publication and after exchange. Both scenarios and their parent fail. All original and corrected attempts remain preserved.

Five of six publication scenarios initially failed: changed candidate bytes, identical replacement children, or changed ownership-journal bytes could allow publication. Eight failed events include their parents; one scenario already passed. Final publication validates the original journal receipt and exact prepared inventory.

Version 2 .preparation.jsonl journals append a terminal candidate handoff before export. The record binds the candidate name, prepared identity, original workspace inventory, and original child identities. Version 1 journals remain readable only for private preparation recovery.

Staging retains its journal after render cleanup. Normal cleanup checks the original journal receipt. Recovery accepts only remaining entries from the prepared candidate or exchanged original inventory and never selects the live workspace path.
Preparation cleanup refuses a pending replacement journal. Replacement recovery settles first, then preparation recovery completes its remaining cleanup.

Eight process-exit cases cover first and replacement installation, prepared and installed states, and four replacement-journal phases. Other tests cover changed candidate and backup files, malformed handoffs, partial cleanup, and version 1 compatibility.

The first broad race run exposes one integration failure: restoring the old workspace leaves the preparation journal. recoverWorkspace now coordinates both protocols, and the existing exact-tree and completed-cleanup assertions remain intact. A focused follow-up passes ten events, including semantically equivalent journal edits.
The focused boundary run passes 81 events without skips. The final full race result includes the later malformed-handoff, partial-cleanup, and compatibility cases.

The Go policy check, source prose, and Linux/Windows AMD64 compilation checks pass. Compilation does not qualify native execution. Source prose precedes added tests without comments and matches the final documentation.
Journals retain the existing 32 MiB, 120000-event, four-tree, and bounded-scan limits. Incomplete or unrecorded ownership remains preserved, including an empty enclosure after journal removal.

Temporary publication records, legacy relocation, evidence and discovery staging, generation retention, history compaction, twelve mapped subcases, full task verification, review, native CI, and merge remain open.

A concurrent tooling migration changed AGENTS.md, Makefile, go.mod, go.sum, and scripts/verify.sh after the final race run started. Those edits remain outside this commit. Tests and compilation retain their original module source; an additional goago check passes under the migrated tooling. Revalidate the final merged module graph at task qualification.
The first canonical prose check reported one nine-sentence paragraph against the six-sentence limit. A paragraph split preserves its content, and the final check passes.

The final canonical prose check passes. Its source snapshots retain observed tooling edits separately from the six owned documentation files. Plan maintenance preserves task criteria, invariants, scope, and the goal block.
